questions.stem: Which statement best separates watertight from weathertight?
options: They mean the same thing
Watertight is for openings on deck; weathertight is for bulkheads
Watertight prevents water passing in either direction under a head of water; weathertight keeps water out in any sea condition but need not withstand sustained pressure
Weathertight is stronger than watertight
questions.explanation: A watertight bulkhead or door is built to hold water back under pressure; a weathertight hatch or door keeps out spray and green water. The deck openings are weathertight, the compartment boundaries below are watertight.

options: The entry of sea water through an opening into the hull or superstructure of an undamaged vessel
Water entering through a hole in the hull after a collision
Water running off the deck through the freeing ports
The settling of the vessel at the stern
questions.explanation: Downflooding is water coming in through an opening such as a door, vent or air pipe that has gone under because of heel. Water coming through a damaged hull is flooding from damage, and drainage through freeing ports is the opposite.

options: The angle at which the deck edge goes under water, whatever the openings
The angle at which GZ is greatest
The angle of heel at which the first opening that cannot be closed weathertight goes under water
The angle of list when the bilges are flooded
questions.explanation: The downflooding angle is set by the first unprotected opening to be submerged. The deck edge angle is a separate matter, and the angle of maximum GZ is a point on the GZ curve.

questions.stem: A box-shaped hull has a beam of 5.0 m and a freeboard of 0.50 m. At about what angle of heel does the low-side deck edge go under?
options: About 11.3 degrees
About 5.7 degrees
About 45 degrees
About 84 degrees
questions.explanation: tan(angle) = freeboard / half the beam = 0.50 / 2.5 = 0.2, so the angle is 11.3 degrees. Using the full beam gives 5.7 degrees. 45 would need freeboard equal to half the beam.

questions.stem: A vessel is loaded deeper. What happens to her freeboard and to the angle at which the deck edge goes under?
options: Freeboard decreases and the angle increases
Freeboard increases and the angle decreases
Neither changes
Both decrease
questions.explanation: Loading deeper reduces freeboard, and tan(angle) = freeboard / half the beam, so the deck edge goes under at a smaller angle. Reserve buoyancy also falls.

questions.stem: An engine-room door sill is 0.40 m above the deck and 1.2 m from the centreline of a box hull with 0.30 m of freeboard. If the door were left open, at about what angle would water start to enter?
options: About 14 degrees
About 30 degrees
About 18 degrees
About 60 degrees
questions.explanation: The sill is 0.30 + 0.40 = 0.70 m above the waterline and 1.2 m off the centreline, so tan(angle) = 0.70 / 1.2 = 0.583 and the angle is 30.3 degrees. 14 degrees uses the freeboard alone (tan = 0.30 / 1.2), which is when the deck edge goes under, and 18 degrees uses the sill height alone (tan = 0.40 / 1.2).

questions.stem: Under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001, who must ensure the applicable load lines are not submerged, and what is the maximum fine?
options: The owner only; a fine of up to $5,000 in total
The master; a fine of up to $500,000 for each centimetre or part of a centimetre submerged, or imprisonment up to 18 months, or both
The harbour authority; imprisonment up to 5 years
Every crew member; a fine of $500 for each tonne overloaded
questions.explanation: Section 110(2) puts the duty on the master, and s. 122 sets the penalty at up to $500,000 for each centimetre or part of a centimetre that a load line is submerged, or up to 18 months in prison, or both.

questions.stem: Under the Small Vessel Regulations, what must the owner of a vessel other than a pleasure craft do when making a change that affects watertight integrity or stability?
options: Nothing, as long as the master approves
Inform the harbour authority only
Wait one year and then report the change
Inform the Minister, because it is a major modification
questions.explanation: Section 710 requires the owner to inform the Minister of a major modification, which includes a change affecting watertight integrity or stability. Section 714 requires the design to maintain watertight integrity and prevent downflooding.

questions.stem: At sea in a seaway, which practice best protects watertight integrity?
options: Keep exterior doors, hatches, ports and vents closed and dogged, and keep freeing ports and scuppers clear
Hook open the engine-room door for ventilation and watch the sea state
Block the freeing ports so water cannot come in through them
Open the hatches to let any water drain down
questions.explanation: Open doors and vents become downflooding points as soon as the vessel heels enough. Freeing ports must stay clear so deck water can leave. Blocking them or opening hatches makes flooding worse.
